recipes.title: Choose an editor for layered images and retouching
recipes.description: Start with the kind of artwork and editable files you must deliver; painting, photo retouching and vector work need different strengths.

picks.label: Photoshop document handoff
picks.reason: Layered compositing and retouching fit a workflow that exchanges editable Photoshop documents.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and cloud-feature allowances add cost; test required plug-ins and file round trips.

picks.label: Combined design application
picks.reason: Pixel, vector and layout studios suit a mixed design workflow with a free core application.
picks.tradeoff: A Canva account is required and optional AI features depend on paid plans; verify client file exchange.

picks.label: Open-source raster editing
picks.reason: A capable candidate for local raster editing when an open-source workflow matters.
picks.tradeoff: Check the exact adjustment, color-management and Photoshop interchange requirements.

picks.label: Painting and illustration
picks.reason: Brush-focused drawing tools suit illustration and digital painting.
picks.tradeoff: A painting workflow is different from photographic catalog management or a full Photoshop handoff.

recipes.title: Choose a RAW photo development workflow
recipes.description: Evaluate representative camera files, image organization, tethering needs and the full licensing model before selecting a converter.

picks.label: Local catalog and batch editing
picks.reason: Combines a local photo catalog with repeatable RAW development.
picks.tradeoff: A subscription is required, and Classic uses a different storage model from cloud-centered Lightroom.

picks.label: Tethered studio work
picks.reason: Tethered capture and controlled color editing suit supported studio camera setups.
picks.tradeoff: Check camera support and plan differences; a perpetual license has different update rights.

picks.label: Optical corrections with perpetual licensing
picks.reason: Camera/lens corrections and RAW processing make it a candidate for a purchased-version workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Test exact camera and lens support, GPU requirements and edition-specific features.

picks.label: Open-source photographic workflow
picks.reason: Non-destructive RAW processing suits a local open-source photo workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Its processing model and learning curve differ from commercial editors; test your own images.

picks.label: Detailed RAW development
picks.reason: A useful candidate for detailed RAW conversion and adjustment.
picks.tradeoff: Choose a separate organizational workflow when its catalog features do not match your archive.

recipes.title: Choose a video editor for real project delivery
recipes.description: Use representative footage and required export formats; timeline compatibility, color work and hardware matter more than a universal ranking.

picks.label: Editing with color and finishing
picks.reason: A candidate when editing, color and finishing need a coordinated production workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Free and Studio capabilities differ, and GPU, codec and platform support need checking.

picks.label: Adobe timeline exchange
picks.reason: Fits teams that deliver editable Premiere projects and connect to Adobe post-production tools.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and project-sized CPU, GPU and storage needs add cost.

picks.label: Open-source nonlinear editing
picks.reason: A general timeline editor for users who want an open-source editing workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Evaluate effects, proxy behavior and export results using the intended footage.

picks.label: Independent desktop editing
picks.reason: A candidate for straightforward editing and media workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Complex collaboration and project exchange may require a different editor.

recipes.title: Choose tools for motion graphics and visual effects
recipes.description: Separate animated design, node compositing and three-dimensional scene creation before comparing applications.

picks.label: Layered motion design
picks.reason: Keyframed layers, animated text and tracking suit motion-design compositions.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription, preview memory and render time matter; a video editor is still useful for final assembly.

picks.label: Node-based compositing
picks.reason: A node workflow suits assembling image operations into a visual effects graph.
picks.tradeoff: Check the required effects, plug-ins and production maintenance needs.

picks.label: Three-dimensional scenes and rendering
picks.reason: Use it when the shot needs models, animation, rendered scenes and compositing in one package.
picks.tradeoff: Learning a 3D production environment can be disproportionate for a simple title animation.

recipes.title: Choose a desktop office suite
recipes.description: Compare required document fidelity, spreadsheet features, collaboration rules and supported operating systems using real files.

picks.label: Microsoft desktop compatibility
picks.reason: Choose when the work depends on Microsoft desktop application features and editable Office handoffs.
picks.tradeoff: Use a plan that includes installed apps; recurring cost and Windows/Mac differences remain.

picks.label: Open-source local office work
picks.reason: A full local office suite is useful when open formats and independent desktop editing are priorities.
picks.tradeoff: Complex Office documents, macros and layouts need file-by-file compatibility checks.

picks.label: Office-format editing workflow
picks.reason: A candidate for editing familiar document, spreadsheet and presentation formats on the desktop.
picks.tradeoff: Confirm required macros, accessibility and complex document features before replacing an established suite.

recipes.title: Edit PDFs or turn scanned pages into searchable documents
recipes.description: Identify whether the job is editing existing content, recognizing scans, rearranging pages or running repeated document transformations.

picks.label: Broad PDF editing workflow
picks.reason: Combines PDF editing, conversion and signing for Acrobat-based document exchange.
picks.tradeoff: Requires a subscription; optional AI and service features can have separate entitlements.

picks.label: OCR-focused conversion
picks.reason: A candidate when converting scanned layouts into searchable or editable documents is the main task.
picks.tradeoff: Mac and Windows editions differ; automated CLI/RPA use has separate license conditions.

picks.label: Repeatable searchable-PDF processing
picks.reason: Adds recognition to PDF workflows when a command-line pipeline is appropriate.
picks.tradeoff: It does not provide a general visual editor for the original page content.

picks.label: Page organization
picks.reason: Focused page arrangement can be sufficient for joining, reordering or splitting documents.
picks.tradeoff: Choose another tool for OCR or editing text inside a page.

picks.label: Many PDF operations in one interface
picks.reason: A candidate for a broader set of document transformations through one interface.
picks.tradeoff: Deployment, edition and component licensing need review; assess any server exposure.

recipes.title: Explore business data and build visual reports
recipes.description: Compare local authoring separately from publishing and team distribution, because those capabilities often have different licenses.

picks.label: Free Windows report authoring
picks.reason: Build and inspect local Power BI data models and report pages without a paid desktop authoring license.
picks.tradeoff: Windows-only desktop; organizational publishing and service sharing require separate entitlements.

picks.label: Visual exploration on Windows or Mac
picks.reason: The current Free Edition supports local visualization and database/file analysis.
picks.tradeoff: Free Edition is for the user’s own internal analysis: no exchange of Tableau content, client outputs or Cloud/Server access; registration and possible reconnection apply.

picks.label: Visual analytical pipelines
picks.reason: Graphical workflows suit exploratory data analysis and modeling.
picks.tradeoff: It serves a different purpose from enterprise dashboard publishing and governed report distribution.

picks.label: Programmable and reproducible analysis
picks.reason: Notebooks combine code, explanations and plots for custom data work.
picks.tradeoff: Requires programming and an explicit process for sharing or deploying interactive reports.

recipes.title: Choose a numerical or symbolic computing environment
recipes.description: Begin with existing code, mathematical methods and required toolboxes; symbolic algebra and numerical engineering are related but distinct needs.

picks.label: Established engineering toolchain
picks.reason: Fits laboratories, courses and engineering code that require MATLAB and specific toolboxes.
picks.tradeoff: Toolboxes and deployment products can add licenses; Mac and Linux capabilities require checking.

picks.label: Open-source numerical scripting
picks.reason: A candidate for numerical work and compatible portions of MATLAB-style code.
picks.tradeoff: Proprietary toolbox behavior and complete MATLAB compatibility are not guaranteed.

picks.label: Integrated symbolic notebooks
picks.reason: Combines symbolic mathematics, numerical evaluation and interactive technical documents.
picks.tradeoff: Paid use-class terms and optional online-service entitlements apply.

picks.label: Open-source mathematical environment
picks.reason: Brings several mathematical systems into a programmable open-source workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Installation and differences between underlying systems can require more setup.

picks.label: Focused symbolic algebra
picks.reason: A candidate for symbolic manipulation without a full commercial technical-computing subscription.
picks.tradeoff: Compare notebook, plotting and specialized function needs separately.

recipes.title: Choose CAD for drawings, parametric parts or manufacturing
recipes.description: Pick by the deliverable: a DWG drawing set, a parametric model, a scripted shape or a manufacturing workflow.

picks.label: DWG production drafting
picks.reason: Fits projects with AutoCAD-specific drawings, conventions and tooling.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription or Flex cost and Windows/Mac toolset differences matter.

picks.label: Focused two-dimensional drafting
picks.reason: A candidate when precise 2D drawings are the main output.
picks.tradeoff: Community and Professional editions differ; verify required file formats and tools.

picks.label: Connected design and CAM
picks.reason: Combines product modeling with manufacturing preparation in one connected workflow.
picks.tradeoff: Personal-use eligibility is restricted, and extensions or commercial use can require payment.

picks.label: Open-source parametric modeling
picks.reason: Fits a desktop workflow that values editable parametric models and an open-source environment.
picks.tradeoff: Validate workbench maturity, geometry and exported files against the intended production process.

picks.label: Programmatic solid geometry
picks.reason: Useful when repeatable geometric design is best expressed as code and parameters.
picks.tradeoff: Its script-based workflow is less suited to direct freeform sculpting or drafting.

recipes.title: Automate repeated Windows desktop tasks
recipes.description: Choose between visual flows, scriptable input and tested automation; account for UI changes and error recovery.

picks.label: Visual application workflows
picks.reason: Records and composes desktop or browser actions with a Microsoft automation environment.
picks.tradeoff: Included attended use has limits; sharing, cloud orchestration and unattended runs need appropriate licenses.

picks.label: Custom shortcuts and input scripts
picks.reason: Fits keyboard shortcuts, text automation and small custom Windows scripts.
picks.tradeoff: Scripts need maintenance and explicit handling of focus, timing and application changes.

picks.label: Structured automation suites
picks.reason: A keyword-driven framework suits repeatable flows with reusable libraries and reports.
picks.tradeoff: Library selection and a development environment add setup compared with a recorded desktop flow.

recipes.title: Run Windows applications on a Mac
recipes.description: Verify the Mac CPU architecture, guest operating system and the actual application before choosing a VM product.

picks.label: Integrated Mac desktop workflow
picks.reason: Guided guest setup and desktop integration suit frequent use of supported Windows applications.
picks.tradeoff: Paid product; Windows licensing is separate, and Apple-silicon guest/application limitations remain.

picks.label: No-charge Fusion route
picks.reason: Fusion is the Mac member of VMware’s currently free desktop hypervisor family.
picks.tradeoff: Broadcom account downloads and guest support checks are required; Workstation is the separate Windows/Linux host product.

picks.label: Open-source Mac virtualization interface
picks.reason: A candidate for managing supported virtualized or emulated operating systems on a Mac.
picks.tradeoff: Virtualization and cross-architecture emulation have different performance and compatibility tradeoffs.

recipes.title: Prepare editable vector artwork and page layouts for collaborators
recipes.description: The requested delivery format and publication structure should determine whether you need vector illustration, typesetting or a combined design app.

picks.label: Native Illustrator vector delivery
picks.reason: Fits scalable artwork when collaborators specifically require Illustrator files and workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription; document exchange still needs testing for fonts and effects.

picks.label: Structured publication production
picks.reason: Fits books, magazines and multipage publications requiring InDesign handoff.
picks.tradeoff: Subscription and publication training add cost, and linked assets must be managed.

picks.label: Combined vector and layout work
picks.reason: Offers vector, pixel and layout studios in one free-core application.
picks.tradeoff: Requires a Canva account and verification of the requested interchange formats.

picks.label: Open-source SVG artwork
picks.reason: A candidate for scalable vector drawings centered on SVG workflows.
picks.tradeoff: Complex Illustrator-specific effects and long-document typesetting are different requirements.

picks.label: Open-source page layout
picks.reason: A candidate for desktop publishing when a local open-source workflow is preferred.
picks.tradeoff: Evaluate typography, print settings and handoff requirements on the actual publication.
